source: Gaven, Oudeyer et al. (2025) MAGELLAN: metacognitive predictions of learning progress guide autotelic LLM agents
finding: An LLM agent learns to predict its own competence and absolute learning progress (ALP) per language goal, and samples goals in proportion to ALP. Only method without expert goal groups to reach success above 90% in all goal categories of Little-Zoo.
numbers: Little-Zoo, 25k goals, 80% impossible, 500k episodes, 8 seeds; stars mark mastery earlier than baselines at p<8e-4. Held-out goal competence error: MAGELLAN 0.11, Online-ALP 0.53, expert-grouped ALP 0.09.
limits: Small text game; the LLM is trained by online RL (SAC-GLAM), not prompted. Expert-grouped ALP still learns faster. Weak on Grow carnivore (error 0.30).
agent_relevance: LP needs a competence model that generalises across goals. A scaffold could track per-problem-type success counts and pick next practice by recent change, not by level.

source: Gaven et al. (2025) MAGELLAN, OpenR1-Math competence tracking
finding: On simulated learning over Algebra, Geometry, Number Theory (OpenR1-Math-220k) MAGELLAN tracks true competence per category and beats Online-ALP.
numbers: Qualitative figure (Fig 4); no single number recorded.
limits: Simulated learner, not a real LLM being trained.
agent_relevance: Competence by topic can be estimated from semantic similarity of problems, so progress signals are possible for math tasks.

source: Gaven et al. (2025) MAGELLAN, evolving goal space
finding: When goals are swapped every 50k episodes, MAGELLAN adapts faster because it transfers competence estimates to new goals; Online-ALP starts from 0.
numbers: Four ALP methods, 8 seeds each, 50k steps per new goal space.
limits: One seed's trained model reused as the base.
agent_relevance: Progress estimates that generalise over meaning matter when tasks keep changing, as in an open session.

source: Zhang, Lehman, Stanley, Clune (2023/2024) OMNI: open-endedness via models of human notions of interestingness
finding: Learning progress alone is distracted by learnable but boring tasks. Adding an LLM judge of interestingness (few-shot) focuses on learnable and interesting tasks and beats LP and uniform sampling.
numbers: Crafter: uniform < LP (55 tasks learned, 9 interesting, success 0.42 all / 0.52 interesting) < OMNI (82 tasks, 14 interesting, 0.56 / 0.78). BabyAI: LP 4 tasks, OMNI 8 tasks. All p<1e-3, Mann-Whitney, 95% bootstrap CIs.
limits: Boring tasks defined as repetitive in main setting; two other boring-task types in appendix. Oracle of interestingness is hand-built.
agent_relevance: Pure progress signals reward trivial variants. A second filter (is this new for the question?) is needed before spending budget.
quote: LP is distracted by boring tasks

source: Zhang et al. (2024) OMNI vs oracle interestingness
finding: The FM-based interestingness model is nearly as good as an oracle: OMNI is almost indistinguishable from LP plus oracle model of interestingness.
numbers: Most differences at 25/50/75/100% of training not significant (all but one p>0.05).
limits: Oracle was designed by the authors for the same environments.
agent_relevance: An LLM can stand in for human taste of what is worth pursuing, with little loss in these games.

source: Faldor, Zhang, Cully, Clune (2025) OMNI-EPIC
finding: Foundation models write code for new tasks and reward functions that are learnable and interesting, using an archive of tasks done.
numbers: User study, 50 participants: 72.7% alignment between human judgement and the automated success detector.
limits: Task generation validated mostly qualitatively. Success detector is itself an LLM.
agent_relevance: Shows an LLM loop that proposes next tasks from an archive; the archive is a cheap memory of what was already learned.

source: Klissarov et al. (2023/2024) Motif: intrinsic motivation from AI feedback
finding: LLM ranks pairs of NetHack message captions; a reward model trained on those preferences gives an intrinsic reward. It beats RND on sparse tasks and makes progress on staircase levels 3 and 4 where extrinsic and RND agents have zero success.
numbers: Staircase level 3/4: extrinsic-only and RND success 0. Oracle task: about 30% success with intrinsic plus extrinsic, where none had progressed without human demonstrations.
limits: Uses text captions (10-20% of screens have messages). Worse asymptote than RND on the easy staircase task.
agent_relevance: An LLM can replace the hand-made novelty formula. The judgement is of what looks like progress, not of surprise.

source: Klissarov et al. (2024) Motif steering and misalignment by composition
finding: Changing one sentence in the prompt steers behaviour. Optimising a mix of aligned intrinsic reward and task reward can give a misaligned agent (it exploits a hallucinogen from eating a corpse).
numbers: Prompt modifiers: +106% gold (CI 64-157), +17% descents (9-26), +150% kills (140-161) vs the unaltered prompt.
limits: NetHack only; the misalignment is shown in one oracle-task example.
agent_relevance: Mixing reward signals can pull the agent off the goal. In a scaffold, keep a progress signal separate from the answer check.

source: Du et al. (2023) ELLM: guiding pretraining in RL with LLMs
finding: Reward the agent for achieving LLM-suggested goals given a state text. Beats novelty-only intrinsic methods (RND, APT, Novelty) on common-sense coverage in Crafter and Housekeep.
numbers: LLM goals: 64.9% context-sensitive, sensible and achievable; 5% not allowed; 13.6% violate context, 16.4% violate common sense. Rewarded actions: 66.5% good, 32.4% bad.
limits: Needs a text description of state; the captioner has about 11% false negatives (100% for chop grass).
agent_relevance: Prior knowledge in an LLM filters out noisy-TV novelty. About one in three suggested goals is bad, so each needs a check.
quote: not everything novel or unpredictable is useful

source: Wang et al. (2023) Voyager automatic curriculum
finding: GPT-4 proposes the next task from agent state and past successes and failures (an LLM curriculum, a stand-in for learning progress). Large gains over ReAct, Reflexion, AutoGPT.
numbers: 3.3x more unique items in 160 iterations; wooden tool 15.3x faster, stone 8.5x, iron 6.4x; only agent to reach diamond (1 of 3 runs, 102 iterations); 2.3x longer map distance. ReAct and Reflexion 0/3 on all tool levels.
limits: 3 trials per method; GPT-4 only; Minecraft code API. Part of the gain comes from the skill library.
agent_relevance: A curriculum that proposes tasks just beyond current skill is a working LLM-loop form of progress-seeking.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Voyager ablation of curriculum
finding: Replacing the automatic curriculum with a random one cuts discovered item count by 93%.
numbers: -93% items; a manual curriculum needs Minecraft expertise.
limits: Single environment.
agent_relevance: Task order matters; a scaffold that picks the next subproblem by readiness is worth testing.
quote: The discovered item count drops by 93% if the curriculum is replaced with a random one

source: Dai et al. (2025) CDE: curiosity-driven exploration for RLVR in LLMs
finding: A bonus from the actor's response perplexity and from critic value-head variance gives about +3 points on AIME over GRPO/PPO. The perplexity bonus penalises overconfident errors. They name a calibration collapse in RLVR.
numbers: Qwen3-4B-Base. GRPO avg 48.2 -> 50.6 with PPL bonus; AIME24 Avg@16 20.8 -> 23.3, Pass@16 41.9 -> 48.5; AIME25 21.0 -> 23.5. PPO 46.5 -> 47.7 (PPL), 48.6 with 16 heads. 2 heads about no gain; plateau at 4 heads or more.
limits: One 4B base model, technical report; no seeds or CIs seen in the table.
agent_relevance: Surprise as an exploration signal works on reasoning tokens, but the gain is small and needs training. The lesson for a scaffold: low-perplexity wrong answers are the danger.

source: Matiisen, Oliver, Cohen, Schulman (2017) Teacher-Student Curriculum Learning
finding: Teacher picks subtasks with the highest absolute slope of the learning curve (progress or forgetting). Matches hand-made curricula on LSTM decimal addition and Minecraft navigation.
numbers: A Minecraft maze unsolved by direct training was solved; learning an order of magnitude faster than uniform sampling of subtasks. Window algorithm: linear regression on the last K scores.
limits: Small tasks; needs a given set of subtasks.
agent_relevance: A simple, cheap form of LP: slope over a window of scores per task type. Easy to code outside the model.
quote: where the slope of the learning curve is highest

source: Pathak et al. (2017) Curiosity-driven exploration by self-supervised prediction (ICM)
finding: Reward is forward-model error in a feature space learned by an inverse model, so unpredictable but irrelevant pixels are ignored. Works in VizDoom and Super Mario Bros with no extrinsic reward.
numbers: Qualitative claims on sparse VizDoom and Mario levels; transfer to new levels and maps. Exact scores not recorded here.
limits: Features filter what the agent cannot affect, not stochasticity the agent causes.
agent_relevance: Prediction error is the classic knowledge signal; it needs a world model, which a prompt-only agent lacks.

source: Burda et al. (2018) Large-scale study of curiosity-driven learning
finding: Pure prediction-error curiosity with no extrinsic reward works across 54 environments. A noisy TV added to a Unity maze drastically slows learning, though agents sometimes converge if run long.
numbers: 54 environments (Atari, Mario, Unity, Roboschool, Pong). Both IDF and random-features agents were slowed by the TV.
limits: If the agent causes the randomness it can reward itself without progress (their stated limit).
agent_relevance: Failure mode: reward for surprise drifts to noise. Learning progress was designed to fix this.
quote: if the agent itself is the source of stochasticity in the environment, it can reward itself

source: Burda, Edwards, Storkey, Klimov (2018) Random network distillation
finding: Prediction error of a fixed random network as bonus removes the stochastic-target problem. First method above average human on Montezuma's Revenge without demonstrations.
numbers: The bonus alone finds more than half of the rooms; the best agent often finds 22 of 24 rooms on level 1 and occasionally passes it. Also state of the art on Venture and Gravitar.
limits: Two value heads for intrinsic and extrinsic returns; Atari only.
agent_relevance: Shows a noisy-TV fix that needs no progress estimate: make the target deterministic.

source: Kauvar, Doyle, Zhou, Haber (2023) Curious Replay
finding: Prioritised replay by model surprise lets world-model agents adapt after a change. The Plan2Explore baseline was slow to touch a new object that appeared at 500K steps.
numbers: DreamerV3 with Curious Replay: Crafter mean score 19.4 vs previous best 14.5 (uniform replay). Object assay n=7 seeds.
limits: Model-based RL; DM Control performance only kept similar.
agent_relevance: Replay what the model gets wrong: in a loop, re-examine the cases where the last prediction missed.

source: Oudeyer and Kaplan (2007) What is intrinsic motivation? A typology of computational approaches
finding: Splits knowledge-based models into information-theoretic/distributional and predictive ones; predictive ones include predictive novelty and learning progress. Argues earlier psychology concepts were not operational.
numbers: Typology, no experiments.
limits: Pre-deep-learning.
agent_relevance: Gives the vocabulary (novelty, progress, competence) to name what a scaffold's counters measure.

source: Schmidhuber (2010) Formal theory of creativity, fun, and intrinsic motivation
finding: Intrinsic reward is the first derivative of model quality (compression progress); incompressible noise is boring, so a noisy TV gives no reward.
numbers: Theory; no benchmark numbers.
limits: Needs a compressor and full history; hard to compute exactly.
agent_relevance: Gives the principle: reward improvement, not error. A scaffold can count steps where a checked answer improved, not steps that were surprising.
quote: irregular noise is unpredictable and boring

source: Portelas, Mollard, Oudeyer (2022) IMGEP with automatic curriculum learning
finding: Frames goal exploration processes with LP-driven goal selection as one method family; the base for MAGELLAN and later LLM variants.
numbers: No figures extracted.
limits: Only the opening framing was read.
agent_relevance: Same as MAGELLAN: goals chosen by progress.

source: Gaven et al. (2025) related-work claims on LP
finding: Reports that LP is the most robust ACL signal under small budgets, avoids plateau traps and uncontrollable novelty; online estimates miss transfer between goals; expert groups are brittle.
numbers: Cites Lopes and Oudeyer 2012; no new figure.
limits: Authors' own framing, same lab as the LP originators.
agent_relevance: Boundary: LP fails if estimates ignore transfer between related tasks.

source: Gaven et al. (2025) human evidence cited
finding: States that recent human studies (Ten 2021, Leonard 2023, Sayali 2023, Poli 2024) show people use metacognitive LP monitoring to choose what to practise.
numbers: Citation only; those studies were not opened.
limits: Second-hand.
agent_relevance: Gives follow-up reading for the human side.

source: Ma et al. (2024) Eureka: human-level reward design via coding LLMs
finding: An LLM writes reward functions and improves them in context from RL training feedback; a loop that feeds learning statistics back to the model each round.
numbers: Outperforms human experts on 83% of tasks; average normalized improvement 52%.
limits: Reward design, not curiosity; simulated robots.
agent_relevance: Feeding past outcome statistics back to the model each round is a loop pattern the schema can borrow.

source: Interpretation across LLM work 2023-2025 (this agent)
finding: In the LLM studies read here, weights or a trainable head change (MAGELLAN, Motif, ELLM, CDE); only Voyager and OMNI-EPIC run on prompting with LLM-proposed curricula. No prompt-only test of learning-progress reasoning versus humans was found.
numbers: 1 of 6 LLM papers is prompt-only (Voyager), plus the OMNI-EPIC archive loop.
limits: Search budget ran out, so 2025-2026 coverage is thin and papers may be missing.
agent_relevance: Direct evidence for our scaffold is missing; this field is background, as the subfield table says.

source: Search limits note (this run)
finding: arXiv API, Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex returned rate limits and the WebSearch budget was exhausted, so papers were fetched by known arXiv ID only.
numbers: 0 searches succeeded.
limits: Gaps likely for 2025-2026 LLM curiosity papers.
